title: GLP-1R assay roles — the 16 assays that had no description, classified by the UNCHANGED D-152 rule as a new audit layer
question: Now that ChEMBL 37 descriptions exist for the 16 assays D-152 filed as UNKNOWN / BLOCKED_BY_DATA_ACCESS, which role does the frozen rule give each of them, and what would that change?
author: Claude, for Mariusz (mariusz8789-sudo)
authorisation: Mariusz, 2026-10-03 02:35Z: use the 16 missing assay descriptions to update the assay-role classification; do not change D-151/D-152 historically; if the new information changes the interpretation of any assayId, record it as a new audit/decision layer, never by rewriting sealed evidence.
orderOfWork: Committed alone, before any of the 16 descriptions is passed through the classifier. The author has seen ONE of the 16 descriptions (CHEMBL1246709) while inspecting the file format; no classifier has been run on any of them.

theRule.classifier: packages/backend/src/campaign/glp1rEndpointScope.mjs::classifyAssayRoleScoped — the D-152 rule, imported, not copied, not edited
theRule.inputConstruction: Exactly as scripts/glp1r-d152-endpoint-scope.mjs builds it: record = { assayType, description, bao, format } from the assay record; actionType = the A1 action type recorded for that assay, or '' when none.
theRule.fieldMapping: ChEMBL's assay_type -> assayType, description -> description, bao_format -> bao, bao_label -> format. These are the same four fields the D-151/D-152 transcriptions carry.
theRule.noRuleChange: No regular expression, threshold, role, ordering or ambiguity rule is touched. If any of the 16 descriptions does not fit the rule cleanly, the rule's own answer — including UNKNOWN / CONFLICTING_SIGNALS — is the answer.

sourceData.files: docs/evidence/source-data/glp1r-2026-10-03/chembl/assay/<id>.json, fetched from www.ebi.ac.uk ChEMBL 37 (release 2026-05-01) on 2026-10-03 by the ingest thread, raw
sourceData.verification: Every file's sha256 is recomputed and compared with SOURCES.json before use; a mismatch aborts.
sourceData.expectedSetIsD152sBlockedList: Identical to glp1r-d152-endpoint-scope.sealed.json -> assays.blockedByDataAccess. If the fetched set differs, the run aborts with ASSAY_SET_MISMATCH.

whatIsReported: per assay: the new role, the rule's reason, the endpoint sentences it read, species and heterologous-system flags, row count in the combined set, standard types
per role: how many of the 16 went where
the counterfactual totals of the FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM arm if these 16 were added to D-152's 320 rows / 206 compounds — REPORTED, not adopted

whatIsNotChanged.D151_D152: Their sealed artefacts and per-assay role files are not edited. This layer sits beside them.
whatIsNotChanged.D153: D-153's sealed MODEL_GATE_PASS on the 320-row arm stands exactly as sealed. If this audit moves rows into FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM, the enlarged arm is NOT validated here: re-validating on it needs its own preregistered decision, written before that run. Changing the training set of a sealed model after the fact is what this clause forbids.
whatIsNotChanged.gate: glp1r-validation-gate.json is not read for any purpose other than confirming it is unchanged.

allowedOutcomes.NO_INTERPRETATION_CHANGE: All 16 stay outside FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM (UNKNOWN for a new reason, OTHER_FUNCTIONAL or BINDING_AFFINITY). D-152's functional arm is unaffected.
allowedOutcomes.INTERPRETATION_CHANGED: One or more of the 16 classify as FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM. The audit records which, and how many rows and compounds that would add, and says plainly that D-153 is not re-run under this decision.
allowedOutcomes.BLOCKED_BY_SOURCE_DATA: A description is missing or a hash does not match.

boundary: A classification of 16 assays with a rule frozen on 2026-09-30. No model is trained, no gate is read for thresholds, no candidate is touched, nothing sealed is edited.
